svg.text: claudia creates — editing the template (E10.4; branch real-world-docs)
Format ▸ Template… (Ctrl+Alt+E), or a name in the slide's template line. The canvas becomes the template; every change is one command and restyles every slide at once.
D · The template editor: layouts and their slots
Same window, same menus: the canvas shows the template instead of a slide, under an apricot band that says so. Done (or Esc) goes back to the slide it came from.
— changes apply to all 7 slides of this presentation
Drag a slot to move it; it snaps to the grid (50 units). The bar's Slot button adds one; Delete removes it — slides keep their text as free objects.
Title — one per layout; the slide's name in lists and outlines
Text — paragraphs and lists, in the slot's style
Picture — an image or an SVG, with its description
Chart · Table · Formula — later, as those objects come
Notes are not a slot: every slide has them (E10.2)
Changing a slot here changes it on the 1 slide with this layout,
in one step that one undo takes back.
What every slide shares and no slide can change: page format and the repeated items.
Running items are text in a style of the
change with the colours and fonts.
A page format change re-flows every slot;
free objects keep their place relative to
the page and are listed if they fall off it.
Panel B's “Make a named variant…”: a layout that differs from its base in one named way.
New variant of Content and picture
A variant inherits everything else from its base: change the base, and the variant follows.
It is listed under its base (panel D) and in the layout picker; this slide uses it at once.
The name is asked for, never made up: it says what the variant is for (as for styles, D75).
